title: Harmanpreet Hit Three Sixes in One Over at Lord's. India's Women Still Went Home.
excerpt: India posted their highest-ever T20 World Cup score against Australia — and it wasn't enough. Perry and Gardner's century stand knocked India out at the group stage.
body:
Harmanpreet Kaur walked off Lord's Cricket Ground on Sunday having played one of the best innings of her career — 56 off 27 balls, including a hat-trick of sixes off Australian captain Sophie Molineux — and it still wasn't enough.

India's women were knocked out of the T20 World Cup after Australia chased down 171 with an over to spare, a six-wicket victory powered by half-centuries from Ellyse Perry and Ashleigh Gardner that extended the most lopsided rivalry in women's cricket.

The result meant India finished third in Group A despite winning three of their five matches. South Africa, who beat Bangladesh earlier in the day, claimed the second semi-final spot on net run rate.

## The Match


![Cricket Ground — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/49/Sydney_Cricket_Ground_%2824509044622%29.jpg)


India won the toss and batted first, knowing a big total was their only route to the knockout stage. Openers Smriti Mandhana (38) and Shafali Verma (34) delivered a 66-run opening stand that set the tone. Jemimah Rodrigues added 34 but struggled to accelerate and was retired out — a controversial call that will be dissected in the coming days.

Then Harmanpreet took over. The Indian captain arrived with intent and delivered fireworks — six fours, three sixes, a strike rate of 207. Her assault on Molineux in the final over, three consecutive sixes, lifted India to 170-4, their highest-ever score against Australia in a Women's T20 World Cup match.



> **"Assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate said there was "a little bit of disbelief" in the men's camp."**


It felt like enough. For about 19 overs, it was not.

Australia lost Georgia Voll in the second over to a superb Renuka Singh inswinger, and at 54-2 after the powerplay, India had a foothold. But Perry (56 off 38) and Gardner (53* off 29) put on a devastating 100-run fourth-wicket stand that swallowed the target whole. Gardner finished it with an over to spare.


![Sophie Molineux — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/07/2018%E2%80%9319_VW_v_SAS_18-09-22_Molineux_%2801%29.jpg)


## Deepti's Record

Amid the defeat, Deepti Sharma etched her name into history. With her wicket in the match, she surpassed the legendary Jhulan Goswami to become the highest wicket-taker in women's international cricket — 356 wickets across all formats. In a tournament defined by India's near-misses, it was a milestone that deserved a bigger stage.

## Kohli and Anushka in the Stands

Adding to the Lord's atmosphere, Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma were spotted in the stands, cheering on the women's team. Former India coach Ravi Shastri was also in attendance. It was a rare gathering of Indian cricket royalty at the Home of Cricket — a moment that spoke to how far women's cricket in India has come, even if the result was familiar.


![Ellyse Perry — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/2017%E2%80%9318_W_Ashes_A_v_E_Test_17-11-09_Perry_portrait_%2802%29.jpg)


## What It Means

India's women have now failed to win a T20 World Cup title despite reaching the semi-finals or later stages in multiple editions and winning the ODI World Cup last year. The tournament continues without them — Australia face West Indies and England play South Africa in the semi-finals at The Oval.

For the diaspora fans who packed Lord's on a sunny London afternoon — many of them British Indians who had turned the ground into a wall of blue — the double blow was brutal. India's men had lost the T20 series to Ireland just hours earlier, making June 28 one of the most painful days in recent Indian cricket memory.

India's men head to England for a five-match T20 series starting July 1. The women head home to regroup. The wait for a maiden T20 World Cup continues.

## The Semi-Final Lineup

The tournament moves to The Oval for the semi-finals: Australia face West Indies, and hosts England take on South Africa. Australia, six-time champions and unbeaten in the group stage, remain the overwhelming favourites. India had beaten South Africa, Bangladesh, Pakistan, and the Netherlands in the group but could not overcome the one team that has haunted them across tournament after tournament.

The scheduling of the India-Australia match also drew controversy earlier in the week. India's fate was partly determined by the South Africa-Bangladesh result earlier in the day — a match India had no control over. Had Bangladesh held on, India would have qualified regardless of their own result against Australia. That scheduling quirk, which forced India to play the last match of the group with their destiny partially in other teams' hands, will be examined by the ICC's competition committee.

For Indian cricket, the symmetry of the day was painful. Both the men's and women's teams lost on the same afternoon — the men whitewashed 2-0 by Ireland in Belfast, the women eliminated at Lord's. Assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate said there was "a little bit of disbelief" in the men's camp. In the women's camp, the feeling may be closer to frustration — they had done everything right except beat the one opponent that mattered most.
